paths.description: Public mobile sign-in entry: inspect first viewport, rendered semantics, form attributes, user preferences, responsive layout, headers/network, and raw no-JS response. Represents only the unauthenticated gateway.
Authenticated feed, profiles, search, messaging, groups, media, settings, and account flows. Not covered because a real account is required.
Signup and business-page creation flows. Not covered to avoid creating accounts or submitting personal/business data.
conditions: user data and possible account creation required

findings.summary: The sign-in page continues a non-essential animation when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion raw-CDP probe found one running animation with a 1500ms duration and no prefers-reduced-motion CSS rule; the reduced-motion screenshot is evidence/home-reduced.png.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce override that removes or shortens non-essential animations and transitions.

findings.summary: At least one important control has a touch target below the recommended size.
findings.evidence: The rendered-control probe measured the country/code button at 24x48 CSS pixels, while the adjacent controls are 44-48px tall.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase the country selector hit area to at least 44x44 CSS pixels without reducing its visible focus treatment.

findings.summary: The small sign-in surface has a slow and request-heavy observed load.
findings.evidence: Navigation timing reported loadEventEnd at about 3826ms and 193 resource entries. Lighthouse was attempted but failed with NO_FCP, so field-equivalent LCP/INP/CLS values remain blocked.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the critical path, prioritize the sign-in UI, and defer analytics and nonessential application bundles until after the form is usable.

findings.summary: A minimal login screen initiates an excessive dependency surface.
findings.evidence: The raw-CDP network capture recorded 204 requests and 201 responses, including about 149 responses from st.vk.ru and multiple analytics origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Ship a minimal authentication bootstrap, defer noncritical scripts, and remove or lazy-load dependencies not required to render and submit sign-in.

findings.summary: The unauthenticated sign-in page contacts a broad tracking and analytics surface before user action.
findings.evidence: The rendered probe observed 14 third-party origins, including scorecardresearch.com, mail.ru analytics, tns-counter.ru, apptracer.ru, mradx.net, ads.vk.com, and stats.vk-portal.net. Raw headers also set long-lived SameSite=None identifiers.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit every pre-consent third party, remove nonessential trackers, and delay optional analytics until a lawful user choice or a necessary in-context event.

findings.summary: The sign-in document lacks semantic heading and landmark structure.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM probe found no h1/h2/h3 elements and no main, nav, header, footer, or explicit landmark roles on the primary sign-in view.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark the sign-in region as main, expose “Sign in to VK” as the h1, and preserve a logical keyboard order with visible :focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: The viewport declaration prevents user zoom.
findings.evidence: The live DOM reports minimum-scale=1.0, maximum-scale=1.0 and user-scalable=no in the viewport meta tag.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale, minimum-scale, and user-scalable=no so users can zoom; retain width=device-width and initial-scale=1.

findings.summary: The raw server response does not expose the rendered sign-in content to non-JavaScript clients.
findings.evidence: Raw HTML contained only an “Your browser is out of date” warning, while the browser-rendered view contained the VK sign-in form and legal/help links.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a progressively enhanced sign-in document with the same meaningful heading, form purpose, and links in server HTML, then enhance it with JavaScript.

findings.summary: The mobile host does not provide a valid sitemap response at its conventional endpoint.
findings.evidence: GET https://m.vk.com/sitemap.xml returned a 430KB HTML page rather than XML; robots.txt was available and the page canonical points to https://vk.com/.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a valid XML sitemap or explicitly reference the canonical host sitemap from robots.txt, and keep mobile/canonical indexing signals consistent.

findings.summary: The entry page exposes no Open Graph or structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM probe found no Open Graph properties and no JSON-LD blocks, despite the page representing the VK organization/service.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph tags and Organization/WebSite JSON-LD that match the visible page and canonical URL.

findings.summary: The CSP is extremely broad and permits unsafe script execution patterns.
findings.evidence: The main response is HTTPS with HSTS, but script-src includes both unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval plus a long allowlist of third-party script origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Move to nonce/hash-based scripts, remove unsafe-eval and unsafe-inline, and reduce connect/script allowlists to origins needed by the sign-in surface.

findings.summary: Several modern defensive response policies are absent.
findings.evidence: The captured main response includes HSTS and X-Frame-Options but no Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or X-Content-Type-Options header; CSP also permits unsafe script patterns.
findings.suggestedFix: Add strict Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and nosniff headers, then harden CSP and prefer frame-ancestors as the clickjacking policy.

findings.summary: The core sign-in purpose is not resilient in the raw non-JavaScript response.
findings.evidence: The raw response presents an outdated-browser warning and no sign-in form, whereas JavaScript/browser execution produces the full login UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the essential sign-in form and recovery links with native form behavior, then layer client-side state and validation on top.

findings.summary: “Save user” is selected by default on a sign-in form.
findings.evidence: The initial screenshot shows the Save user checkbox checked before interaction, while the page also sets long-lived identifiers.
findings.suggestedFix: Default the persistence choice off, explain what will be saved and for how long, and let the user opt in deliberately.

findings.summary: The phone sign-in identifier disables autocomplete.
findings.evidence: The live form probe reports input type=tel, name=login, autocomplete=off.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the appropriate sign-in autocomplete token, typically username or tel, and use one-time-code on the verification field rather than disabling autocomplete.

findings.summary: The login page performs disproportionate background network work.
findings.evidence: A first-load capture recorded 193 resource entries and requests to numerous analytics endpoints before any user action.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unnecessary background requests and defer low-priority analytics until after the critical sign-in interaction or an explicit user choice.

findings.summary: Third-party script and tracking cost is disproportionate to the sparse login view.
findings.evidence: The page visually contains a single compact form but contacts 14 third-party origins and records about 200 network responses.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict third-party budget for authentication pages, retain only necessary fraud/security services, and defer the rest.

taskList.title: Minimize pre-action tracking and third-party traffic on the authentication page
Harden CSP and complete defensive response policies
Server-render a progressively enhanced, crawlable sign-in experience
Restore zoom and semantic page structure
Respect reduced motion and remove the remaining login animation under reduce
Make persistence opt-in and enable sign-in autofill
Add accurate share metadata for the public entry page
